Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about ATS optimization

What is an ATS (Applicant Tracking System) and how does ATS score work?
An ATS (Applicant Tracking System) is recruiter resume screening software used by over 90% of companies to filter job applications. It scans resumes for relevant keywords, proper formatting, and job description matching. The ATS score represents how well your resume matches a specific job description — a higher score means your resume is more likely to pass the automated screening and reach a human recruiter.
Is this online resume builder with ATS score really free?
Yes, our ATS resume checker is 100% free with unlimited scans. No sign-up, no credit card, no hidden paywalls. Unlike competitors who limit you to 1-5 free scans, we offer unlimited resume analysis forever. Our free ATS resume builder tools process everything in your browser for complete privacy.
How to create an ATS friendly resume online?
To create an ATS friendly resume: use standard section headers (Experience, Education, Skills), include keywords from the job description, avoid tables/images/graphics, use a clean single-column layout, save as PDF, quantify achievements with numbers, and use our free resume score checker to validate your resume before applying.
Which resume format is best for ATS?
The reverse-chronological format is the best resume format for ATS systems. Use clear section headers, standard fonts, no columns or tables, and avoid headers/footers. A simple, clean PDF format works best. Our ATS resume format checker validates all these elements automatically.
How to improve ATS score of resume?
To improve your ATS score: match keywords from the job description exactly, use standard section headers, include both spelled-out terms and acronyms (e.g., 'Search Engine Optimization (SEO)'), add quantified achievements, remove graphics and complex formatting, and use our resume keyword optimizer tool to identify missing terms.
Can ATS reject good resumes?
Yes, ATS systems can reject well-qualified candidates if their resume isn't properly formatted or lacks specific keywords. Common reasons include using images/graphics, non-standard fonts, tables, missing keywords, creative formats, or saving in incompatible file types. Our free ATS resume checker helps identify and fix these issues before you apply.
What is the difference between an AI resume builder and an ATS resume checker?
An AI resume builder helps create resume content using artificial intelligence, while an ATS resume checker scores your existing resume against job descriptions for compatibility. Our tool combines both approaches — it analyzes your resume against ATS rules, suggests missing keywords, and helps optimize your content for maximum ATS compatibility, functioning as both a resume score checker and an AI resume improvement tool.
Does this tool work for freshers and experienced professionals?
Yes, our ATS resume tools work for everyone — fresh graduates, experienced professionals, career changers, and industry specialists. The ATS scoring engine adapts to any experience level, and our domain converter helps tailor resumes for specific industries like IT, banking, finance, marketing, and more.
What's considered a good ATS score?
A score above 70% indicates your resume is well-optimized for ATS systems. Above 80% is excellent and means you have strong keyword alignment with the job description. Below 50% means significant changes are needed — focus on adding missing keywords, fixing formatting issues, and restructuring sections to match standard ATS expectations.
How long does the ATS resume analysis take?
Our analysis is instant — typically under 1 second. Because everything runs locally in your browser using JavaScript, there's no server processing delay. Your results appear immediately after clicking 'Analyze' with detailed keyword matching, formatting checks, and improvement suggestions.
Is my resume data safe and private?
Absolutely. Your resume never leaves your device. All processing happens 100% in your browser using client-side JavaScript. No data is uploaded to any server, stored in any database, or used to train any AI model. We don't use cookies to track your resume content, and there's no account system storing your documents.
PDF vs Word — which format is better for ATS?
Clean, text-based PDFs are the safest choice for ATS systems. Avoid scanned-image PDFs as ATS can't read them. Some older ATS systems prefer .docx, but modern systems handle both well. Our tool accepts PDF uploads and parses them locally using Mozilla's open-source pdf.js library to extract text accurately.
Can I use images, colors, or graphics in my ATS resume?
Avoid images, charts, logos, and complex graphics in ATS resumes. Most ATS systems cannot parse visual elements, so any information contained only in images will be lost. Minimal color use for headings is generally safe, but keep the overall design simple and text-based. Our ATS checker flags these formatting issues automatically.
How many keywords should I include in my resume?
Aim to naturally incorporate 60-80% of the important keywords from the job description. Don't keyword-stuff — ATS systems and recruiters can detect unnatural repetition. Focus on hard skills, technical tools, certifications, and industry-specific terms. Our Keyword Analyzer tool identifies exactly which terms you're missing and suggests where to add them.
What file formats are supported for upload?
We support PDF file uploads. When you upload a PDF, it's parsed entirely in your browser using Mozilla's pdf.js library — no server upload occurs. If you have a Word document, you can also paste the text directly into the text area. This gives you the most flexibility while maintaining complete privacy.

How to Optimize Your Resume for ATS

Most large companies use Applicant Tracking Systems to filter resumes before a human recruiter ever sees them. These systems scan for relevant keywords, proper formatting, and structured content. If your resume doesn't meet their criteria, it gets filtered out — regardless of your qualifications.

Online Resume ATS helps you understand how these systems work and what you can do to pass them. Our tools are completely free, run entirely in your browser, and never store your data on any server.

What Makes a Resume ATS-Compatible?

An ATS-friendly resume follows a few core principles: use standard section headers like "Experience," "Education," and "Skills." Avoid tables, multi-column layouts, images, and headers/footers — these confuse most parsing engines. Save your resume as a clean PDF (not a scanned image), and always include keywords that match the job description you're applying to.

Our ATS Score Checker compares your resume directly against a job description. It identifies which keywords you're missing, flags formatting problems, and gives you a clear score with specific suggestions to improve.
